metadata.document_title: Keel Plan v5 Addendum 6: DeepSeek Harness Full Teardown (Architecture, Packages, UI/UX, Builder Rules, CI)
metadata.document_intent: Adds only items not already in Master Plan and Addenda 1-5. Free-only. Milestones follow v5. Every row names its source.

prefix_legend.D: Derived from the DeepSeek Harness (clean-room behavioral reimplementation in Python).
prefix_legend.V: Own ideas (builder protocol in Section 9), tagged [S].
prefix_legend.C: Conflict/decision rows in Section 11; metadata only, not feature rows.

tag_legend.[T:key]: Read this session (21 Nov 2026) in that file. Behavior is reimplemented clean-room in Python (X0.10). Never copy code, names, icons or prompts.
tag_legend.[S]: My suggestion, no repo behind it.

read_status.note: Package map comes from DS-AGENTS's own layout table; apps/* contents and each package README are unread (conflict C-12). Treat all DS package-level claims as [T:DS-AGENTS] summaries only until M0 reads them.

metadata.adaptation_rule: dsh is TypeScript on a framework called Cordis (Node >= 24.9, pnpm). Keel is a Python daemon + Electron renderer. Nothing in dsh's stack is adopted; only behaviors and design rules.

clean_room_specs.stack_adoption: None. Clean-room behavioral reimplementation only; no dsh code, names, icons or prompts are copied.
clean_room_specs.reimplementation_target: Keel Python daemon (X0.10) + Electron renderer; Keel service registry keys: sessions, system_prompt, tools, agents, agent_loop, llm.
clean_room_specs.config_is_data_only: Do NOT adopt dsh's !!js config feature (which allows code in config files). Config stays data-only; conditional composition via overlays/profiles only (conflict C-11).
clean_room_specs.tier2_non_replaceable: Tier 2 safety services are plugins that cannot be replaced or disabled by profiles/patches (D1.1 exception, conflict C-10).
clean_room_specs.model_visible_equals_logged: Every model request must be reconstructable from the session log; new model-visible input requires a session event; plugins register pure message projections (D2.11).
clean_room_specs.boundary_validation: Trust types inside the process; validate at parser/config, queued messages, model/tool JSON, durable files and worker/process/wire boundaries (D6.8).
clean_room_specs.licensing_note: dsh is MIT; SDK runtime wheel per platform must verify license/size (D1.8).

reading_list: docs/cookbook/* (adding a package, tool, LLM adapter, settings card; extension cookbook)

m0_reading_list: docs/subsystems/* (session, tools, scope, core, llm-streaming, system-prompt, subagent, agent-team, conversation, working-directory)
docs/cookbook/* (adding a package, tool, LLM adapter, settings card; extension cookbook; reviewing persistence type changes)
.agents/skills/* (especially dsh-client-ui-ux, dsh-error-handling, dsh-pre-push-checks, dsh-create-upgrade-guide, dsh-session-projection, dsh-pr-description, dsh-prose-standard)

conflicts_with_earlier_plans.issue: dsh requires 100% per-file coverage and a very large gate set; a solo owner with a free-tier CI may not afford the minutes (Master Section 8, CI row).
conflicts_with_earlier_plans.resolution: Adopt gates in tiers: security-critical modules 100%, everything else graded; run heavy lanes on release tags and locally. Record in `DECISIONS.md`.

conflicts_with_earlier_plans.issue: dsh is explicitly "not secure, not production-ready, developer preview"; Keel's goal is a shippable product.
conflicts_with_earlier_plans.resolution: Copy the honesty (D5.x) but keep Keel's Tier-2 and approvals as hard requirements; do not use "preview" as an excuse for skipping security tests.

conflicts_with_earlier_plans.issue: dsh makes plugins everything, including the safety layers (replaceable by patches).
dsh's `!!js` config feature allows code in config files.

metadata.builder_protocol_for_own_ideas: For every V row (and any [S] row): (1) one-paragraph why + 2 similar products/standards by category; (2) free/license check with date; (3) spec in Keel's words; (4) smallest slice behind an experimental flag; (5) negative tests first if security-relevant; (6) end-to-end evidence incl. offline run; (7) owner review before default-on if it stores new personal data, uses network, or changes approvals.
priority_order: Builder constitution and gates: D6.1-D6.12, D6.15, D6.16, D6.25, D7.1, D7.12, V16
Safety copy and onboarding: D5.1-D5.5, V17
Everything else at its milestone; P2 after the v1.0 candidate is green. All rows enter PLAN-INDEX.json with their source tag.
uncertain_or_normalized_rows: D6.1-D6.25: Section 7 table has columns ID | Rule | Gate? | M; no Priority or Source column. Priority set to null; source set to T:DS-AGENTS from the section heading; Rule mapped to feature, Gate? mapped to detail.
V16-V23: Section 9 table has columns ID | Idea | Approach for the builder | M | Pri; source set to S ([S] own idea) per Section 9 heading and Section 0 tag legend.
C-8..C-12 are conflict/decision rows, captured as metadata only, not counted as features.
C-12: apps/* and each package README are unread; all DS package-level claims (D3.11-D3.23) are [T:DS-AGENTS] summaries pending M0 verification.
D3.11: 'ptc-runtime' meaning explicitly 'to be verified' in the source document.

acceptance_criteria are derived heuristically: explicit test/gate/check clauses from each row are extracted when present; otherwise a generic implement-and-verify criterion is generated. They are not verbatim source text.

references/dependencies are parsed from cross-reference tokens in feature/detail text (e.g. W1.1, C5.5, X6.8, Master 9); dependencies are the subset preceded by dependency phrasing such as 'builds on', 'extends', 'backed by'.
